limitations: Experimental MQTT3.1.1 QoS0/1/2 implementation; core QoS2 tests are not a complete normative conformance matrix or production release approval.

QoS2 Method B routes at first accepted PUBLISH before PUBREC. Duplicate QoS2 PUBLISH by Packet ID only resends PUBREC; completion frees ID for a new exchange. No cross-system business exactly-once guarantee.

Receiver record count and bytes are separate quotas, with full original message retained until PUBREL; no eviction/expiry of admitted persistent exchanges. Lower-QoS subscribers and business observations retain their weaker semantics.
Snapshot format2 reads legacy format1 and upgrades before listen. Old binaries cannot read format2; no in-place downgrade.
Linux/WSL2 x86_64 only; SIGKILL is not real device power-loss testing. Existing SQLite FULL/DELETE/exclusive full-image and deferred shutdown-Will boundaries remain.

One early concurrent phase test failed at startup using inherited150ms Request timeout; isolated rerun passed. New phase-correctness fixtures now use2s; existing150ms lost-reply/uncertainty tests remain. Both diagnostic logs retained; final full check passed.

Store and protocol implementation has no new dependency or framework rev change. Private task Cargo cache used; source hashes capture cumulative uncommitted workspace inputs and exclude evidence directories.
Metrics fixed-name count grows to36; metrics and Admin audit remain memory-only. No policy/certificate hot reload or encrypted database.
unresolved: CompleteMQTT3.1.1 normative conformance and broader interoperability/fault matrix.
F7 MQTT5 properties/reason codes/session and message expiry/receive maximum/shared subscriptions.
Optional WebSocket and Bridge, production storage throughput/recovery SLO, hardware power-loss, cross-platform and independent Agent/release MUST gates.
Immediate durable Will publication at host shutdown remains deferred recovery as documented in F5; requires a separate pre-shutdown drain design.
